newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat closes mostly lower, contract lows set.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat closes mostly lower, contract lows set.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter closed mostly easier with contract lows set across the board as the market continued its long-term slide.

Dealers noted the weather was almost ideal for hard red winter wheat growth and development while there also continued to be concern that export prospects appear dismal with U.S. wheat still seen as overpriced.

Some talk circulated that Argentinian wheat could be imported into the United States with the cost of shipping it to the U.S. Gulf at about $155 per ton, compared with the current prices for HRW at the U.S. Gulf of around $180 to $185.
"The numbers crunch but I don't think it will be done," one trader said, noting any attempt to import would meet a hostile response from U.S. farmers.
December wheat closed 4-3/4 cents lower at $4.15-1/4 a bushel after setting a contract low of $4.15. Other months closed one cent higher to two cents lower.
Estimated volume on KCBT wheat totaled 22.6 million bushels, the KCBT reported.
